\label {sol: self adjoint part of a star vector space is a real vector space}This is clear, because the involution is an $\R$-linear map. Of course, $0$ is self-adjoint, which we now show quickly. Observe that:
\[\forall x \in V: x+\dual{0} = \dual{(\dual{x}+0)} = \dual{(\dual{x})} = x.\]
This implies that $\dual{0}$ is an identity for addition in $V$ and since identities are unique, we see that $0$ is self-adjoint.
